::: {.callout-note}
## Meeting location

The 2027 meeting will be held at USC's University Park Campus. The specific
building will be announced before the meeting. Check current transit schedules,
fares, and parking rules when planning your trip.
:::

## Best ways to reach USC

### LA public transit

Metro is usually the simplest way to reach campus without dealing with USC
parking. The Metro E Line serves USC at Expo/Vermont, Expo Park/USC, and
Jefferson/USC.

- From Santa Monica, Culver City, and other Westside locations, take the E Line
  directly toward downtown Los Angeles.
- From UCLA or Westwood, take a local bus, Santa Monica Big Blue Bus, or Culver
  CityBus connection to the E Line.
- From Los Angeles Union Station, take the Metro B or D Line to 7th St/Metro
  Center, then transfer to the E Line.
- Other Metro rail and bus routes connect with the E Line throughout Los
  Angeles County.

Use a TAP card or the TAP app and check [Metro](https://www.metro.net/) for the
best route on the day of travel.

### Intercity rail

Amtrak and Metrolink are good options for attendees traveling from outside
central Los Angeles.

- **From Santa Barbara, Ventura, or the San Fernando Valley:** use Amtrak's
  Pacific Surfliner or Metrolink's Ventura County Line.
- **From Orange County or San Diego:** use the Pacific Surfliner or Metrolink's
  Orange County Line.
- **From the Inland Empire and other regional locations:** use the applicable
  Metrolink line.

Most intercity trips arrive at Los Angeles Union Station. From there, take the
Metro B or D Line to 7th St/Metro Center and transfer to the E Line for USC.
Train frequency varies, especially on weekends, so check schedules in advance.

### Driving and parking

If you drive, use a live navigation app for the best route. Traffic near
downtown Los Angeles, I-10, and I-110 can change quickly.

You have two practical parking options:

#### Park at USC

Visitor parking is available in USC campus structures, generally on a cashless,
first-come basis. Common options include McCarthy Way, Figueroa Street, Downey
Way, Royal Street, and USC Shrine. The planning estimate is approximately $20
per day, but rates and availability can change.

Check USC's current parking instructions before arriving. Nearby street
parking is limited and often metered or permit-restricted.

#### Park at Metro and ride in

Parking at a Metro station and taking the E Line can be cheaper and easier than
driving onto campus. Metro parking is often about $3 per day, plus train fare;
some lots may be free on weekends or holidays.

Useful E Line park-and-ride options west of USC include:

- La Cienega/Jefferson
- Culver City
- Expo/Sepulveda
- Expo/Bundy
- Expo/Crenshaw

Travelers from other directions can park along the A or B Line and transfer to
the E Line. Ride to Expo Park/USC or Jefferson/USC. Check current lot prices,
hours, and availability before choosing a station.

## Nearby lodging

- [USC Hotel](https://uschotel.usc.edu/) is adjacent to campus.
- Downtown Los Angeles and LA Live have many hotels with convenient Metro
  access to USC.
- Koreatown and Culver City offer additional options with transit connections.

These are general suggestions, not reserved conference room blocks.
